sheet-68.description: The southern half of downtown Sea Bright on the narrow barrier beach between the South Shrewsbury River on the west and the Atlantic Ocean on the east, from South Street and St. George Place at the top of the sheet down to Centre Street and the open grounds south of it. The sheet is drawn at 60 ft to an inch with north at the top. Down the middle runs a 150 ft corridor holding West Ocean Avenue, the double track of the Central Railroad of New Jersey and East Ocean Avenue. West of it lie closely built blocks of small frame dwellings along West Church, West New, Surf, Beach and Centre, with Front Street along the river side; this side also has the Sea Bright Freezer cold storage plant, the Monmouth Ice Co. ice houses, the Sea Bright M.E. Church and its parsonage, St. Luke's A.M.E. Church, the fire department engine house and lockup, the Grand Central Hotel, a boarding house, garages, blacksmith and wheelwright shops, and a steam boat landing with a freight house on the river. East of the tracks are fish houses and a steam laundry along East Church and East New, Fisherman's Court, Wayne Street or Sea Side Place with rows of small houses facing the ocean bulkhead, and the railroad freight depot and platform. South of Centre the sheet is mostly open: W. E. Connors stables with an auto house and work shop beside a boat slip on the river, and the large W. E. Connors cottages on the ocean side of Ocean Avenue. Water mains are drawn in most streets.
notes: West Ocean Avenue is modern Ocean Avenue (NJ 36); East Ocean Avenue survives as East Ocean Avenue north of Beach Street, and south of Centre the old East Ocean Avenue line is modern Ocean Avenue.
West Church, West New and Centre are modern Church Street, New Street and Center Street; East Church and East New are East Church Street and East New Street.
Fisherman's Court is modern East Surf Street; Wayne Street or Sea Side Place is modern Wayne Street; Centre east of the tracks is East Center Street.
The railroad corridor (Central Railroad of New Jersey) between West and East Ocean Avenue is gone; part of it is now private parcels between Ocean Avenue and East Ocean Avenue.
Modern Front Street bends east north of Surf Street; the drawn Front Street / West New junction does not match the modern node and was not used.

Printed sheet 68 (N.J. Coast vol. 1), 60 ft to an inch, north up. Southern downtown Sea Bright: South St to Centre and the W. E. Connors grounds south of it; West Ocean Av / railroad / East Ocean Av corridor (150 ft). One part, whole sheet.

sheet-69.description: The northern half of downtown Sea Bright on the barrier beach between the South Shrewsbury River and the Atlantic Ocean, from South Street and St. George Place at the bottom of the sheet north past Rumson Road to the Sea Bright passenger station. The sheet is drawn at 60 ft to an inch with north at the top. The centre of the sheet is the 150 ft corridor of West Ocean Avenue, the Central Railroad of New Jersey and East Ocean Avenue. West of it is the commercial core: brick and frame stores, a drug store, the post office, a bank, a hall and other shops along West Ocean Avenue between Peninsula Avenue, River and South, the Geo. W. Elliott & Co. hay, grain and wood yard with coal bins and a hoisting engine on the river, livery and boarding stables, Stoerer's Express carriage house, a coal yard and Primary School No. 5. North of Peninsula Avenue stand the Pannaci Hotel and the Sea Bright Inn with its cottages, an elevated water tank and an underground gasoline tank. Rumson Road leaves the town westward over the iron bridge across the river. East of the tracks the ocean side holds large resort buildings: the Sea Bright Beach Club with its pavilion and horse shed, the Presbyterian church (closed in winter), Pannaci bath houses, the Peninsula House hotel, cottages and the Hotel Octagon, with bath houses built on piles over the ocean bulkhead. The passenger station stands on the west side of the tracks north of Rumson Road.
notes: West Ocean Avenue is modern Ocean Avenue (NJ 36); River and South are River Street and South Street.
The drawn Rumson Road and iron bridge lie about 75 m south of the modern Rumson Road bridge; that junction was not used.
Badminton Court and Poppi Place, modern streets west of Ocean Avenue, are not drawn; they run along old lot lines.
The Central Railroad of New Jersey and its passenger station are gone.

Printed sheet 69 (N.J. Coast vol. 1), 60 ft to an inch, north up. Northern downtown Sea Bright: South St north past Peninsula Av and Rumson Rd (iron bridge) to the passenger station. One part, whole sheet. Only junctions along Ocean Avenue survive (Rumson Rd bridge moved about 75 m north): helmert from three hand-picked points.
